title: NASA and Russia-China Coalition Race to Deploy First Lunar Nuclear Reactor by 2030s
summary: NASA aims to deploy its Lunar Reactor 1 at the lunar south pole by December 2030 to produce 20 kilowatts for five years of autonomous operation, while Russia and China plan to deploy Selena by 2036 producing 10 kilowatts for ~10 years to power the International Lunar Research Station. Both reactors
takeaways: NASA Lunar Reactor 1: December 2030 deployment target; 20 kilowatts for 5 years
Selena (Russia-China): 2036 deployment; ~10 kilowatts for ~10 years
20 kilowatts equivalent to ~16 US household electricity usage
Lunar night lasts ~2 weeks; reactors provide stable power for exploration and habitation
Russia launched 30+ space reactors since Cold War; US launched only once (1965), never deployed

title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope begins planet-hunting observations

takeaways: Pointing stability: <1/100,000 degree for 30 minutes (Wide Field) or 8 hours (Coronagraph)
Equivalent to aiming laser at dime from ~150 miles away
Coronagraph Instrument received first cosmic light September 22
Wide Field Instrument contains 18 detectors for guide star monitoring
Potential for stability improvement to dime-targeting from ~230 miles

summary: NASA's senior director outlined five space-dominance goals in response to intensifying U.S.-China competition over lunar and Mars exploration. Artemis III (2027) will test commercial lunar landing systems; Artemis IV (2028) will carry Americans to the lunar surface using the proven approach.

Artemis III (2027) will dock with commercial human landing systems from Blue Origin and SpaceX
Artemis IV (2028) will carry Americans to lunar surface

title: NASA Curiosity Rover Captures Detailed Martian Cliff Panorama at Dawn
summary: NASA's Curiosity rover, operational for 13 years, captured detailed panoramas of wind-carved Martian cliffs and boxwork formations—intricate ridge patterns thought to have formed from ancient underground water deposits—on Mount Sharp. The rover has been upgraded for greater autonomy to investigate w
takeaways: Curiosity rover operating 13 years at Mount Sharp (3 miles/5 km high)
Captured panorama at local Martian dawn showing wind-carved cliffs
Boxwork formations span miles; formed billions of years ago by underground water

title: NASA Selects GIMLI Project to Explore Lunar Cave Beneath Marius Hill Pit
summary: NASA selected the GIMLI (Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation) project to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit on the Moon opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube. Led by Planetary Science Institute's Than Putzig, GIMLI will use ground-penetrating radar, seismic sens
takeaways: Project lead: Than Putzig (Planetary Science Institute)
Instruments: ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors, gravity measurements, cameras
Partners: Honeybee Robotics (equipment), Norwegian Space Agency
First use of active-source seismic methods on lunar surface since Apollo
Target: determine if caves/lava tubes exist beneath Marius Hills volcanic region
Caves could provide radiation shielding and temperature protection for future astronauts
Funded through PRISM program with delivery via CLPS initiative

title: NASA Develops Dexterous Humanoid Robots for Lunar Operations and Human Assistance
summary: NASA's Dexterous Robotics Team is developing humanoid robots with fine motor control for lunar and Martian operations. Rather than replacing human explorers, the robots aim to make space exploration safer and more sustainable by conducting high-risk tasks in extreme environments.
